question: What happens to a Christian when they die?
answer: The believer goes at once to be with Christ. Jesus told the dying criminal, "Truly I tell you, this very day you will be with Me in paradise" (Luke 23:43), and Paul wrote that he would "much rather move out of the body and make our home with the Lord" (2 Corinthians 5:8). This is far better than anything here, yet it is not the final ending: at Christ's return the dead will be raised and creation renewed.

question: Will Christians be judged if they are already forgiven?
answer: Those in Christ will never face condemnation: "those who are in Christ Jesus now face no sentence of condemnation" (Romans 8:1), because Jesus bore God's wrath against sin on the cross. Yet every believer will stand before the judgment seat of Christ, "so that each one may receive what matches the things done in the body, whether good or worthless" (2 Corinthians 5:10). This judgment does not decide salvation; it is for reward or loss (1 Corinthians 3:10–15).

question: What will the new heavens and new earth be like?
answer: The Bible ends not with souls in the clouds but with a renewed creation: "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth" (Revelation 21:1). God will live with His people, and "Every tear He will wipe from their eyes. Death will be no more, and no more mourning, no crying, no pain" (Revelation 21:4). Above all, His servants "will look upon His face" (Revelation 22:4), living coram Deo in perfect joy.
